QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_4

question.text: During FY 2025-26, Ms. Priya has the following capital gains and losses: Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG) from equity shares Rs.3,00,000; Short-Term Capital Loss (STCL) from debt mutual funds Rs.1,80,000; Long-Term Capital Loss (LTCL) from gold Rs.2,50,000. Per the intra-head set-off rules (NISM X-B, pp. 162-163), assume Ms. Priya sets off the STCL first against available capital gains and then sets off the LTCL against any remaining LTCG. What is (a) the net taxable capital gain for FY 2025-26 and (b) the total amount of unabsorbed capital loss carried forward to subsequent assessment years?

answer.text: (a) Rs.3,00,000; (b) Rs.4,30,000 - none of these losses can be set off against equity LTCG
(a) Rs.70,000; (b) Rs.1,80,000 - only LTCL is set off, STCL is carried forward separately
(a) Nil; (b) Rs.1,30,000 of unabsorbed LTCL carried forward
(a) Nil; (b) Rs.4,30,000 - total losses are carried forward in full since they exceed total gains

explanation.text: The Logic: STCL can be set off against any capital gain (STCG or LTCG); LTCL can be set off only against LTCG (NISM X-B, pp. 162-163). Applying the sequence prescribed in the stem: (1) STCL Rs.1,80,000 set off against LTCG Rs.3,00,000 -> remaining LTCG Rs.1,20,000; (2) LTCL Rs.2,50,000 set off against remaining LTCG Rs.1,20,000 -> remaining LTCG Nil, unabsorbed LTCL Rs.1,30,000. Net taxable capital gain = Nil; unabsorbed LTCL carried forward = Rs.1,30,000 (for 8 assessment years). Option C is uniquely correct. The Trap: Option A misstates the law (STCL and LTCL CAN be set off against equity LTCG of the same character). Option B is the result of setting off LTCL first and leaving the STCL unabsorbed - not the prescribed sequence. Option D correctly notes the net gain is nil but incorrectly carries forward both losses in full, ignoring the actual set-off against the LTCG. Note: The original item asked only for the net taxable capital gain, with two distractors both arriving at Nil through different reasoning. The stem now asks for BOTH (a) the net taxable gain AND (b) the unabsorbed-loss carry-forward, and explicitly prescribes the STCL-first set-off sequence, so only one option (correct on both parts) can be selected. Source: NISM Series-X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook, pp. 162-163.
